# The 14 books

Each book is a plugin. Install one with `/plugin install <slug>@guided-plugins`. `review` always exists; so do `audit`, `plan`, `checklist`, `fix` and `explain-rule`.

## Presets

A preset is one primary book and up to two secondary books that are rated Complementary with it and with each other. Claude Code installs a preset with `/plugin install guided-<preset>@guided-plugins` (the books and the `guided` plugin).

| Preset | For | Primary | Secondary | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `everyday-code` | Teams writing and reviewing ordinary application code every day. | `clean-code` | `refactoring` | Clean Code decides readability questions; Refactoring adds the safe, small-step way to act on them. |
| `legacy-rescue` | Changing code that has no tests, in a codebase you did not write. | `legacy-code` | `refactoring`, `clean-code` | Working Effectively with Legacy Code gets the change under test first; Refactoring then restructures in small steps; Clean Code names what better looks like. |
| `backend-service` | Services and APIs that must survive production: structure, data and failure. | `clean-architecture` | `release-it`, `data-intensive-apps` | Clean Architecture keeps the dependency direction; Release It! covers timeouts, retries and overload; Designing Data-Intensive Applications covers consistency and data flow. |
| `domain-model` | Business-rule-heavy code where the model of the domain is the hard part. | `ddd-distilled` | `clean-architecture`, `refactoring` | DDD Distilled gives the pragmatic core of domain-driven design; Clean Architecture protects the model from frameworks; Refactoring evolves it safely. |
| `system-design` | Designing modules, APIs and boundaries before or while building them. | `philosophy-of-design` | `clean-architecture`, `code-complete` | A Philosophy of Software Design judges module depth and interfaces; Clean Architecture sets boundaries; Code Complete covers construction detail. |
